mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover 4.4 V8 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned engine replacement for a Range Rover 4.4 V8 typically ranges from £6,500 to £12,000 for supply only, depending on whether it is the petrol (AJ-V8) or diesel (448DT) variant. Used engines start around £2,500 but carry higher risk, while rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing 4.4 V8 engine in a Range Rover?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs in the Range Rover 4.4 V8 are unexplained coolant loss, a sweet smell from the engine bay, or a distinct rattling noise on cold starts pointing to timing chain wear. For the 448TDV8 diesel, watch for oil/coolant mixing or illuminated temperature warning lights.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover 4.4 V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends heavily on the vehicle's overall condition. A typical Range Rover 4.4 V8 holds a UK market value of £3,000-£8,000. If the chassis, bodywork and interior are in pristine, low-mileage condition, a £6,500-£12,000 rebuilt engine is a sound investment to preserve a classic flagship. If the vehicle is heavily worn, evaluate scrap or part-exchange value first, as the rebuild cost may exceed the car's worth.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover 4.4 V8 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Range Rover 4.4 V8 typically takes 3 to 5 days, depending on the specialist's workload and whether any ancillary components like the cooling system are being upgraded simultaneously. Sourcing a quality rebuilt V8 unit may add a few days.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the 4.4 V8 petrol and the 4.4 TDV8 diesel?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Range Rover 4.4 V8 petrol (AJ-V8, 2002-2005) is a naturally aspirated unit prioritising smooth, refined power delivery and simpler mechanical architecture. In contrast, the 4.4 TDV8 diesel (448DT, 2006-2009) is a twin-turbocharged unit focused on massive low-end torque, heavy towing capability, and improved fuel economy, though it carries more complex cooling system components.

historyTimeline.h2: Range Rover 4.4 V8 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the L322 Range Rover 4.4 V8 launched, it brought robust, refined V8 power to the flagship SUV, initially as a naturally aspirated petrol unit before evolving into a highly capable twin-turbo diesel architecture.

milestones.description: Introduction of the 4.4L AJ-V8 naturally aspirated petrol engine (286-299 hp) in the L322 Range Rover, replacing the older BMW M62 unit for improved refinement and JLR integration.
Major powertrain update with the introduction of the 4.4L TDV8 (448DT) twin-turbo diesel engine (306 hp), offering massive low-end torque and improved fuel economy for the heavy L322 platform.
Final year of the 4.4 TDV8 in the L322 generation before the transition to the 4.4 SDV8 (368DT) and later 3.0 TDV6 architectures in the subsequent L405 generation.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Range Rover 4.4 V8 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover 4.4 V8 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 4.4L V8 engines in the Range Rover 4.4 V8 (both the AJ-V8 petrol and 448TDV8 diesel) are powerful and refined, but age-related wear on the cooling system and V8-specific seals is a known pattern. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Cooler & Cooling System Leaks - Why the Range Rover 4.4 V8 448DT Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: The oil cooler is situated in the valley of the V8. Its seals degrade under sustained thermal cycling, leading to oil/coolant mixing or external leaks that can escalate to overheating if undetected.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil cooler seals, coolant crossover pipes, and thermostat; flush system.
repairOptions.longevity: Extends life significantly if caught before overheating damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded cooling components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the engine has already suffered thermal damage or internal seizure.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Range Rover 4.4 V8 of relevant age (2006-2009) currently holds a UK market value of approximately £3,000-£8,000 [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader / Parkers market observations], with pristine, low-mileage Vogues commanding higher premiums. At this value band, a full rebuilt engine replacement (£8,000-£12,000) risks exceeding the vehicle's current market value. Evaluate scrap or part-exchange value carefully before committing to a full rebuild.
problems.recommendation: If your Range Rover 4.4 V8 is showing minor external coolant seepage but has not overheated, a targeted oil cooler and cooling system refresh by a JLR specialist is the most cost-effective route. However, if the engine has already suffered thermal damage, a full rebuilt replacement is the only reliable long-term solution, provided the vehicle's overall condition justifies the investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 448DT Range Rover 4.4 V8 engine prices

problems.group: Coolant Crossover Pipe & Timing Chain Wear
problems.h4: Coolant Crossover Pipe & Timing Chain Wear - Why the Range Rover 4.4 V8 AJ-V8 Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: Plastic coolant crossover pipes become brittle over time, leading to leaks. Concurrently, timing chain tensioners can wear, producing a characteristic rattle on cold starts.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace plastic cooling pipes, water pump, and inspect/replace timing chain tensioners.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective at preventing catastrophic overheating or timing failure if addressed early.

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £6,500-£10,000 [ESTIMATED - using Jaguar AJ-V8 data as proxy]
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded valvetrain and cooling components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended only if chain failure has already caused internal engine damage or the block is cracked.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above, the £2,500-£6,000 value of an older Range Rover 4.4 V8 (2002-2005) makes a full engine replacement financially challenging. A full rebuild often exceeds the vehicle's total market value, making preventative maintenance the most viable path for preservation.
problems.recommendation: Do not ignore a cold-start rattle or minor coolant loss in your Range Rover 4.4 V8. A timely cooling system and tensioner refresh by a specialist is a well-documented fix that preserves the engine's longevity at a fraction of the cost of a full rebuild.
